Name: Elemental Force
Author: poaskkiliaks
Description:
[size=6][b]Elemental Force[/b][/size]

[i]Fourteen elemental spirits, three tiers of power, and one amphora to carry them.[/i]

The Wizard has been watching you. When he finally invites you to the tower, he hands over the [b]Amphora of Elementals[/b] — a vessel that holds the power of the spirits sleeping in the valley's minerals. Everything after that is up to you: infuse the essences, refine them, and decide which powers you carry into the mines each morning.

[line]

[size=5][b]How it goes[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*][b]The Wizard writes to you[/b] once you're on good terms with him (two hearts). Visit the tower and the Amphora of Elementals is yours — two slots to start.[/*]
[*][b]Someone else writes too.[/b] A voice that signs off as [i]???[/i] sends you an essence to get started, and Maru — who has been dreaming about her — turns up on your farm with the blueprint for the [b]Essence Infuser[/b].[/*]
[*][b]Infuse minerals into essences.[/b] One mineral, one clay, five moss, one day.[/*]
[*][b]Use the amphora to open its screen[/b] — the vessel's slots on top, grouped by tier, your inventory below. Click an item, click the slot you want it in. A power is yours for as long as it stays slotted, and you can rearrange the whole set whenever you like. Right-clicking an item onto the amphora in your inventory still works as a shortcut, dropping it in the first free slot of its tier.[/*]
[*][b]Collect all eight essences[/b] and the amphora is upgraded to the [b]Amphora of Echoes[/b] (four slots), while Maru arrives with the [b]Runic Compressor[/b].[/*]
[*][b]Compress five essences into a Shard[/b] — a week of work for a stronger, sharper version of the same spirit.[/*]
[*][b]Collect all eight shards[/b] for the [b]Amphora of Spirits[/b] (ten slots) and the [b]Soul Extractor[/b].[/*]
[*][b]Extract souls from shards[/b] and run whatever combination of ten powers you can afford. The souls remember. They watch. In time they may even speak to you.[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][b]The fourteen spirits[/b][/size]

Each spirit has three tiers, and each tier is its own power — an essence is not a weaker shard, it's a different perk. Nothing stacks by itself: what you carry is what you chose to slot.

[size=4][b]Essences[/b][/size]
Cheap, and most of them only pay off somewhere specific — that is the point. The first amphora has two slots, so you swap them for wherever you are going that morning. Ifrit runs faster, but only under the desert sun; Shiva only in Winter; Titan's defence is the one that works anywhere, always.

[size=4][b]Shards[/b][/size]
Five essences of one spirit, compressed. This is where the powers stop being numbers and start doing things: Leviathan can tilt tomorrow's weather toward rain, Carbuncle can turn an incoming hit aside entirely, and Phoenix sets off a blast when something gets close enough to regret it.

[size=4][b]Souls[/b][/size]
Two shards, extracted — and the scarcest slot in the mod. Ifrit throws fire at whatever is nearest, Shiva freezes what you strike, Carbuncle sends the damage straight back where it came from, and Phoenix puts you back on your feet instead of letting the day end.

[i]Every item says exactly what it does, and by how much, in its own description in game — including the ones that only switch on in a certain place, season or weather. Finding that out is half of it.[/i]

[size=4][b]Eight are asked for. Six are not.[/b][/size]
The upgrade letters only ever ask for eight essences and eight shards. Everything below that line is optional — yours to chase whenever you feel like it, or to ignore entirely.
[list]
[*][b]Cactuar[/b] rewards getting hit rather than avoiding it, and its calling is the only silent one in the mod.[/*]
[*][b]Umbra[/b] is the spirit of sustain: it drains, it pays energy for what falls, and its calling takes instead of giving. It is not refined from a mineral — it takes Void Essence, and Krobus is the one who mentions it exists.[/*]
[*][b]Bismarck[/b] is the only spirit that touches fishing. Two levels of it, treasure that adds to your bait rather than replacing it, and two extra fish on every catch.[/*]
[*][b]Lakshmi[/b] is the only spirit that knows the barn exists. Animals stay content without the morning round, produce comes out a grade better, and the slow producers lose a day while the daily ones give twice.[/*]
[*][b]Odin[/b] is speed in the saddle and nowhere else, heavier blows against the undead, and now and then a strike that simply ends it.[/*]
[*][b]Golem[/b] is the one aimed at the mod itself: it pulls moss out of stone, and moss is what the Essence Infuser eats. Its pickaxe costs nothing to swing, and what you break takes its neighbours with it.[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][b]The three machines[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Essence Infuser[/b] — 1 mineral + 1 Clay + 5 Moss, one day. Crafted from 5 Iron Bars, 20 Coal, 1 Diamond and 1 Oak Resin.[/*]
[*][b]Runic Compressor[/b] — 5 essences of one spirit + 5 Iron Bars + 10 Refined Quartz, seven days. Crafted from 1 Gold Bar, 5 Iron Bars, 3 Battery Packs and 1 Pine Tar.[/*]
[*][b]Soul Extractor[/b] — 2 shards of one spirit + 10 Solar Essence + 5 Void Essence, three days. Crafted from 1 Iridium Bar, 10 Refined Quartz, 5 Battery Packs and 1 Maple Syrup.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Which mineral makes which essence[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Ifrit[/b] — Tigerseye[/*]
[*][b]Shiva[/b] — Slate[/*]
[*][b]Titan[/b] — Bixite[/*]
[*][b]Leviathan[/b] — Ocean Stone[/*]
[*][b]Carbuncle[/b] — Jamborite[/*]
[*][b]Kirin[/b] — Prismatic Shard[/*]
[*][b]Ramuh[/b] — Thunder Egg[/*]
[*][b]Phoenix[/b] — Star Shards[/*]
[*][b]Bismarck[/b] — Celestine[/*]
[*][b]Lakshmi[/b] — Geminite[/*]
[*][b]Odin[/b] — Obsidian[/*]
[*][b]Golem[/b] — Granite[/*]
[*][b]Cactuar[/b] — 100 Cactus Fruit[/*]
[*][b]Umbra[/b] — 100 Void Essence[/*]
[/list]
[i]You do not have to read this list. The valley has notes scattered through it, in a previous bearer's handwriting, that name one mineral each — and the game tells you what it is called in your own language.[/i]

Each recipe arrives with its own visit from Maru, so the machines show up exactly when the amphora is ready for them.

[line]

[size=5][b]The amphora[/b][/size]

Three vessels, each an upgrade of the last — and the slots are not interchangeable. Each vessel reserves them by tier:
[list]
[*][b]Amphora of Elementals[/b] — 2 essences[/*]
[*][b]Amphora of Echoes[/b] — 1 shard + 3 essences[/*]
[*][b]Amphora of Spirits[/b] — 1 soul + 3 shards + 6 essences[/*]
[/list]So the endgame is not fourteen powers at once: it is [i]one[/i] soul out of fourteen, three shards out of fourteen, six essences out of fourteen. Upgrading keeps whatever is already attached. The amphora's screen shows the slots grouped by tier and lists, at the bottom, the effects actually running right now — so a power that is switched off because you're in the wrong place or season is visibly absent instead of quietly doing nothing.

[line]

[size=5][b]Settings[/b][/size]

Every power with a number behind it can be tuned in [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] — chances, damage, durations and recovery rates. If a spirit feels too strong or too shy for your save, the dial is there.

[line]

[size=5][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]SMAPI 4.0.0 or later[/*]
[*]Content Patcher[/*]
[*][b]Mail Framework Mod[/b] — required; the amphora upgrades arrive by letter[/*]
[*]Generic Mod Config Menu (optional, for the settings above)[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]Languages[/b][/size]
English, Português (Brasil), Español, 日本語, 简体中文.

[line]

[size=5][b]Stuck?[/b][/size]

The upgrade letters are checked when a day starts, so you need to be [i]holding[/i] everything they ask for when you wake up — an essence in a chest doesn't count, though one attached to the amphora does. If a letter still won't come, run [font=Courier New]ef_check[/font] in the SMAPI console: it prints every requirement the letter tests, item by item, and says which one is missing.
